subject: Difficulty with large numbers of simulations with function Nmix.gof.test

messages.author: 30c5d1d065585de4
messages.subject: Difficulty with large numbers of simulations with function Nmix.gof.test
parts:
Dear all,

I have been trying to use function Nmix.gof.test to test goodness of fit for a density model. The function has been giving me reasonable answers for up to 99 simulations, but when used with the same data and the same unmarked frame object with 100 or more simulations, it returns "Error in checkForRemoteErrors(val) : 7 nodes produced errors; first error: object 'Area' not found" 

I would appreciate any assistance with fixing this. I did find one earlier discussion about this problem, but the solution proposed there was to use function parboot instead: I would ideally like to be able to run Nmix.gof.test for a larger number of simulations. 

I have attached my code file, and a csv file which is identical in structure to the one I am using (the values are slightly different). 

Sincerely, 
Abhimanyu

messages.author: 4e956cc50ac3e075
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Difficulty with large numbers of simulations with function Nmix.gof.test
parts:
Hi,


taking a quick look at the code and data you sent, here are a few issues I noticed:


-you are using binary data (detected/not detected) for the species data, whereas you are requesting an N-mixture model (i.e., pcount( )) which requires count data. The data type you are using is not appropriate for pcount( ), you should look into occupancy models instead.


-you have quite a lot of explanatory variables on both the abundance and detection parts of the model and the pcount( ) code you sent returns an error (Hessian is singular.  Try using fewer covariates.).


I suggest reconsidering the type of analysis you are using and reading up on the type of data appropriate for these analyses.


Best,


Marc
